items.title: A new connect applies the previous session's terminal status and stops the poll
items.reason: connect() at line 1046 and reloadTunnel() at line 1202 start the health poll before the new extension writes its first status. After any earlier session the status file still holds failed or stopped. A poll tick in the start window applies that old record to the new attempt. The page moves from Connecting to Failed or Idle and stops polling. The extension can then start with no poll watching it. A later Connect tap starts a second attempt and fails on ALREADY_RUNNING. The user cannot stop the running tunnel from the page. The system consent dialog and a cold extension start both make this window long.

items.title: v5.3.5 profiles lose subscription ownership on upgrade
items.reason: Profiles written by the 5.3.5 release carry subscriptionId and no subscriptionStatus. ProfileStore.fromJson sets every absent status to STATUS_USER_CONFIGURED. mergeSubscriptionRun (Subscription.ets:683) skips user-configured profiles. The first 5.4.0 refresh thus never updates or obsoletes the stored subscription rows. It adds a second Active profile for each name and address pair. The old rows stay visible and the subscription loses ownership of them. lld.md:1456 states that no migration exists. The stored shape did gain the status field.

items.title: Session settlement races the extension's own traffic writes and teardown clear
items.reason: handleAction calls settleSessionTraffic before it asks the extension to stop. settleSessionTraffic reads and deletes traffic_stats and writes profiles.json. The extension still runs and writes a cumulative traffic_stats sample once per second (SsVpnExtensionAbility.ets:600). The extension teardown also clears traffic_stats after it writes stopped (SsVpnExtensionAbility.ets:403). A later settle can add the same cumulative counters again. If the teardown clear wins, the session counters are lost. Two processes change the same files with no lock and no owner token.

items.title: A failed settle write leaves PHASE_STOPPING with no exit
items.reason: disconnect() and reloadTunnel() set PHASE_STOPPING and then await settleSessionTraffic without a try block. settleSessionTraffic ends in ProfileStore.addTraffic, which writes profiles.json. A write error rejects the call. The phase stays PHASE_STOPPING and the poll is already stopped. disconnect() returns at its first check, the service button is disabled, and resumeStatus() returns while the phase is PHASE_STOPPING. No page action leaves the state. requirements.md:522 requires an exit for every state. The same gap exists at line 1195 in reloadTunnel().

items.title: Subscription refresh overwrites concurrent profile writes
items.reason: mergeRun reads the full profile list at line 366 and writes it at line 387. It parses every downloaded body in between. A profile save, delete, reorder or Apply Settings write in that window is overwritten. The refresh runs for seconds and the user can edit profiles meanwhile. No version check and no retry protects the write.

items.title: Subscription refresh commits across three files without atomicity
items.reason: mergeRun writes profiles.json, then current_profile_id, then subscriptions.json. A failure after the first write leaves the merged profile list with the old selection and the old updatedAt. The run reports a single store error. lld.md:3867 states that a store error keeps the old file. That statement holds only for the first write.

items.title: A session stopped outside the page is never settled and its counters are erased
items.reason: pollTick moves to Idle or Failed for a stop that the page did not start. It resets the counters and never calls settleSessionTraffic. The sample stays in traffic_stats until the next start clears it at SsVpnExtensionAbility.ets:271. The stored profile counters never include that session. On the core-death path the extension also writes failed with an empty profile id at line 373, so no later settle can attribute the sample. architecture.md:75 lists this risk.

items.title: Custom rules file is read while the UI truncates and rewrites it
items.reason: writeUserRules opens custom-rules-user.acl with TRUNC and then writes it. deployAcl reads the same file in the extension process at every start (SsVpnExtensionAbility.ets:434). No atomic rename and no lock protect the file. A connect during a save can read an empty or partial file. composeCustomRules('') returns [bypass_all]. The session then proxies every destination and ignores the user's rules. A crash during the write leaves the truncation on disk.

items.title: Bare plugin options do not round-trip and gain catalogue defaults
items.reason: ProfileStore.fromJson calls normalizePluginOptions on every load. A profile with a known plugin and empty pluginOpts gets the catalogue default, obfs=tls or mode=websocket. Profile.parseUrl stores a bare plugin with empty options, and seedPluginConfigs keeps it that way. The effective options change after the first reload or save. The file cannot round-trip an empty options text. lld.md:5737 justifies the default only for an old file.

items.title: Subscription store treats an unreadable file as empty and the next save destroys it
items.reason: SubscriptionStore.getAll returns [] for an absent file, a failed read and a JSON error. JsonStore.read returns '' when it cannot open the file. A later add, remove, undo or refresh timestamp write calls saveAll with the in-memory list. Every stored URL is lost. ProfileStore has getAllOrNull for this case. SubscriptionStore has no equivalent.

items.title: Drag after a pending removal moves the wrong profile
items.reason: dragFrom and insertIndex are positions in shown(), which hides pending removals and applies the search. onItemDragMove starts commitRemovals() without await. dropProfile applies the old indices to the whole stored list. ProfileStore.move then renumbers userOrder. A drag while the undo bar is up moves the wrong profile and saves the wrong order. dropProfile refuses a search filter. It does not refuse a pending removal.

items.title: The page and the extension resolve the selected profile differently when it is Obsolete
items.reason: visible() removes Obsolete profiles for the page. Index.currentProfile() falls back to the first visible profile for the connect check, the live counter and the route. ProfileStore.getCurrent resolves current_profile_id against the full list. After a refresh marks the selected profile Obsolete, the page validates one profile and the extension starts another. The live sample then names a profile that no row shows. The merge resets currentId only when it deletes a duplicate.

items.title: JsonStore.read sizes its buffer before it opens the renamed file
items.reason: JsonStore.read calls statSync and then openSync. The extension replaces vpn_status.json and traffic_stats.json by atomic rename every 500 ms to 1 s. A rename between the two calls makes the buffer smaller than the new file. readSync truncates the new JSON. load catches the parse error and returns null. A present status reads as absent. A live sample reads as absent, so the page reports a connect timeout or no traffic after 6 s.

items.title: Export writes the picked file without truncation
items.reason: saveTextFile opens the picked URI with CREATE and without TRUNC. If the URI names an existing longer file, the write starts at offset 0 and leaves the old tail. The exported profiles.json then holds trailing bytes. A later import fails to parse it.

items.title: The refreshed ACL cache is written in place and preferred on the next start
items.reason: refreshAcl opens the cached ACL with TRUNC and writes it in place. deployAcl prefers the cached copy over the shipped rawfile on the next start (SsVpnExtensionAbility.ets:440). A process death during the write leaves a partial cache. A UI read for the GFW import can also see the partial file. The next start then deploys an incomplete ACL. JsonStore uses a temporary file and a rename. This path does not.

coverage.note: Read the requirements state tables and data rules for U01, U02, U03, U04, U05, U06, U07, U08, U09 and U11, the HLD data design and contracts, the LLD state and data sections, and the architecture seams and quality scenarios. Compared them with the product files. Found 15 items: 2 high, 9 medium, 4 low. Checked state transitions, store round trips, cross-process file use and the v5.3.5 to 5.4.0 data migration. No test was run and no device state was observed. Not scanned: docs/oracles, entry/src/test, entry/src/ohosTest, docs/review, native code, pages without persisted state (About, AboutLinks, Network, QrCode).
